p: weary of my life: I am more like a dead man, than to one that lives.
complaint upon myself: I will make an ample declaration of my torments, accusing myself and not God.
condemn me: He would not that God would proceed against him by his secret justice, but by the ordinary means that he punishes others.
good unto thee that thou shouldest: Is it agreeable to your justice to do me wrong?
work of thine hands: Will you be without compassions?
counsel of the wicked: Will you gratify the wicked and condemn me?
flesh: Do you do this of ignorance.
days of man: Are you inconstant and changeable as the times, today a friend, tomorrow an enemy?
wicked: By affliction you keep me as in a prison, and restrain me from doing evil, neither can any set me free.

hands have made me and fashioned: In these eight verses following he describes the mercy of God, in the wonderful creation of man: and on it grounds that God should not show himself rigorous against him.
the clay: As brittle as a pot of clay.
favour: That is, reason and understanding, and many other gifts, by which man excels all earthly creatures.
visitation hath preserved my spirit: That is, the fatherly care and providence by which you preserved me, and without which I would perish immediately.
that this is with thee: Though I am not fully able to comprehend these things, yet I must confess that it is so.
lift up my head: I will always walk in fear and humility, knowing that no one is just before you.
marvellous upon me: Job being sore assaulted in this battle between the flesh and the spirit, breaks out into these affections, wishing rather for short days than long pain.
changes and war are against me: That is, diversity of diseases and in great abundance; showing that God has infinite means to punish man.
cease then: He wishes that God would leave off his affliction, considering his great misery and the shortness of his life.

return: He speaks this in the person of a sinner, that is overcome with passions and with the feeling of God's judgments and therefore cannot apprehend in that state the mercies of God, and the comfort of the resurrection.
order: No distinction between light and darkness but where there is very darkness itself.
